q1_issues.issue: "The broader ... Index" is a comparative, and the instruction set states a comparative does not entail the positive, yet the parse asserts the flat positive `(Member standard_poors_500_index broad)`.

The Measure scale slot is filled with the preposition `off`, which is neither a stated gradable adjective nor a dimension noun, so the amount of a decline is recorded as a dimension named after a particle.

A second Measure on the same entity and same scale `off` carries a different magnitude and unit (0.11 percent), so the two atoms read as conflicting values rather than one amount restated appositively.
The scale symbol `level` appears nowhere in the sentence — "at 1,010.59" states only a number, so the dimension noun is invented rather than read off the surface.
The ticker ".SPX" is dropped entirely, with no atom recording it.

q2_gaps: attributive bare comparative with no stated standard ("the broader Index") — `More` needs two arguments and the positive is not entailed, leaving no licensed encoding
magnitude of a change/decline ("was off 1.07 points") — no licensed scale or head for a delta as opposed to a level
appositive / equivalence "or" restating one amount in a second unit (points vs percent)
a bare numeric value with no stated dimension word ("at 1,010.59") — Measure requires a scale the text does not supply
an alias / ticker symbol appositive (".SPX") for an already-named entity, where a proper noun is allowed exactly one `Name` fact
notes: The name symbol, the separate `(Member ... index)` kind atom for the kind word inside the name, and the `Past (Measure ...)` tense wrapping are all handled per the instruction set.
